title: Monitoring CPU
subtitle: Hardware inventory and per-core utilization — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Report CPU architecture: sockets, cores, threads, NUMA, vendor, model
cards.notes: Inventory of what chips you have — not how busy they are right now. Used to size VMs and taskset.

cards.meaning: Approximately equals logical CPU(s) the OS reports
cards.notes: Check inventory math against the CPU(s) line in lscpu. Thread(s) per core 2 usually means SMT/hyperthreading.

cards.meaning: Memory domains — cores are closer to some RAM than other
cards.notes: RAM is not equally far from every socket. Matters for locality and performance on multi-socket hosts.

cards.meaning: Per-CPU (core) utilization for every logical CPU plus a summary line all
cards.notes: Default report is CPU utilization. No interval means stats since system startup (boot) — a long average, not “right now.”

cards.meaning: Live samples: every 1 second, 5 times (not only boot average)
cards.notes: Same interval/count pattern as sar. Use when you need “busy now,” not since boot.
Application CPU. High user on one core vs all tells you imbalance.
Still user-space, but from processes running at a nicer priority.
Syscall-heavy or kernel work. Pair with user and idle to see where time goes.

cards.meaning: CPU idle while waiting for disk/network I/O
cards.notes: Points to storage or I/O, not “need more CPU.” Fix disks/network before adding cores.

cards.meaning: Time a hypervisor took from this VM (stolen cycles)
cards.notes: Noisy neighbor on the hypervisor. Host contention, not your process list alone.
Idle high = bored. Low idle with high iowait still means waiting on I/O, not compute saturation.

cards.meaning: Time running a guest (typical on a KVM host)
cards.notes: Host-side view of CPU spent inside virtual machines.

cards.meaning: Per-CPU stats: all processors, interval 1 second, count 1 sample
cards.notes: Same utilization story as mpstat. Often from sysstat; can also replay historical data under /var/log/sa/.

cards.meaning: lscpu = what chips you have; mpstat/sar = how busy each core is
cards.notes: Hardware inventory vs utilization. Do not confuse architecture with load.
